newsitem.title: CHINA: China firm wins $1.3 mln damages in court case.
newsitem.headline: China firm wins $1.3 mln damages in court case.

text.p: A north China court has ordered three firms to pay 11 million yuan ($1.3 million) in damages to state-run China State Shipbuilding Corp (CSSC) for improper use of its technology, court officials said on Tuesday.
The Handan Intermediate Court in Hebei province last week ordered the Jiangsu Wuxian Economic and Technological Development Co and two other firms to pay compensation, a court official said.
The other two defendants were Tianjin Land Hydrogen Production Equipment Co and Suzhou Wuxian Hydrogen Production Equipment Co, the official said by telephone.
A research official with China Shipbuilding said the compensation would not cover the company's losses but he believed the decision was acceptable.
"We think the decision has reflected the fairness of the laws, so we will obey it," he said.
China Shipbuilding brought suit in 1994 against the three firms for building hydrogen generating plants using methods CSSC had developed, he said.
Jiangsu Wuxian had hired 28 CSSC engineers and technicians, who then used technology they helped develop at CSSC to build the two water electrolysis plants, the court official said.
"We held discussions with these engineers several times, but with no result. Then we decided to sue," the CSSC official said.
Officials at Jiangsu Wuxian and the other defendants could not be reached for comment.
The court official said the defendants were considering filing an appeal and would have 15 days from the time of the decision to do so.
He did not say how much each of the total compensation would be paid by each of the three firms if they ultimately lost an appeal.
